content: Do measures taking only the values 0 and 1 have a name? Do they have a Mathlib predicate? Mostly out of curiosity.
docs#MeasureTheory.Measure.dirac ?
is there an example of of zero-one measure that's not dirac?
see https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Measurable_cardinal

Weiyi Wang said:

is there an example of of zero-one measure that's not dirac?

I think if your measure space is trivial then there are a bunch more, like the measure that assigns 0 to the empty set and 1 to nonempty sets.
Or maybe more generally, if the measure space is not docs#MeasurableSpace.SeparatesPoints then you could have a Dirac measure that detects a set of points (which aren't separated) rather than a single point

I'm pretty sure in general the docs#MeasureTheory.Measure.dirac doesn't necessarily detect just a single point, it detects the set which is the intersection of all measurable sets containing a particular point
so that would still be a dirac measure
I had a specific example in mind: https://mathoverflow.net/a/466659/147705
I was interpreting "not dirac" as in ∉ Set.range dirac, but if you only compare the measures on measurable sets then I think you're right
measures in mathlib are determined by their values on measurable sets
They have a measureOf : Set α → ENNReal field, so I don't think so, but maybe the axioms force something which I'm not seeing
Ahh docs#MeasureTheory.Measure.trim_le, cool (and hence docs#MeasureTheory.Measure.ext)
How about if s.Countable then 0 else 1, is this a measure?
No, since you can have disjoint uncountable sets

The specific measure I wanted to formalize goes like this. You take α with uncountable cofinality, and define the family of sets which either contains or entirely omits a docs#IsClub set. This is a σ-algebra, and you can define a measure on it where all club sets have measure 1.

Violeta Hernández said:

No, since you can have disjoint uncountable sets

Even if my measure space is the one generated by singletons in an uncountable set?
(it probably has a known name if it's really a measure space)
Edit: this is called the countable-cocountable σ-algebra
Oh, I think that does work.
Violeta, this is the Dieudonné measure that I mentioned to you I was going to formalize so many months ago. I was going to show that its support is empty.
Oh, wow! Did you ever get around to that? If not, mind if I PR it?
I didn't because I had to wait for cofinality to get it's universe issues fixed.

Violeta Hernández said:

Do measures taking only the values 0 and 1 have a name? Do they have a Mathlib predicate? Mostly out of curiosity.

We have MeasureTheory.IsZeroOneMeasure (since a recent PR of @Gaëtan Serré)
Do you know if docs#MeasureTheory.IsZeroOneMeasure.exists_eq_dirac could be upgraded to an iff with StandardBorelSpace α?
Actually StandardBorelSpace can be generalized to MeasurableSpace.CountablySeparated in that lemma (without changing the proof). I'm opening a PR.
#39739
Nice! And I realized it can't be an iff because ⊥ : MeasureableSpace Bool isn't CountablySeparated but does satisfy the theorem
So maybe "countably separates points which can be separated" is the equivalent statement.
I believe the lemma is also true under the assumption that the space is MeasurableSpace.CountablyGenerated, but the proof needs to be changed.

I added a proof for countably generated in the PR. The common property satisfied by CountablySeparated and CountablyGenerated used in the proof is that there is a countable family of sets that generates the atoms of the space.
